subject: Renewal structure: hybrid multi-year + usage-triggered top-up proposal
messages:
From: Sarah Thompson <sarah@oliveanalytics.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal windows + usage-trigger top-up idea

Hannah —

Our finance and platform teams have been reviewing the upcoming renewal and we'd like to propose moving to a 24-month term but with a usage-triggered top-up mechanic rather than a fixed staggered ramp. The goal is to:

- keep unit economics predictable for us in the first 6 months,
- allow headroom for spikes without negotiating mid-contract, and
- avoid a multi-step amendment process later this year.

Specifically, we are thinking: 24 months total, year 1 baseline commit, year 2 baseline + an automatic top-up if monthly usage exceeds 120% of forecast for three consecutive months (top-up applies to the next 3 months and is billed monthly). We still want an annual review and the option to co-term any other Redwood workloads.

Can your team sketch a workable amendment (billing cadence, SLO implications, and an operational trigger that Procurement and Legal can accept)? Attaching our internal forecast and sample SSO audit window.

Thanks,
Sarah
VP, Platform
Olive Analytics

---

Attachment(s): Olive_Forecast_Q4-Q2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), SSO-audit-reqs.pdf (pdf stub)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear framing. We can definitely structure a 24-month term with a measured usage-trigger. A few immediate thoughts:

- "Trigger" mechanics: use a 3-month rolling window >120% of committed monthly baseline to initiate a short-term top-up (3 months). After that, either roll into the baseline at the next annualization point or continue as overage at a reduced incremental rate.
- Billing: monthly invoicing for any triggered top-up so it’s reconciled immediately.
- SLA/Capacity: we can reserve burst capacity through Dedicated burst pools — cost will be higher for guaranteed capacity, or we can provide a best-effort burst with soft SLOs but a lower incremental rate.
- Co-terms: we can include co-term language to align multiple SKUs at the next renewal boundary.

I’ll loop in Karthik for the pricing/technical details and Connor for the mutual action plan and ops handoff. I’ll draft a redline for Legal based on your attachments.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

Sarah / Hannah —

Adding the product/pricing perspective. We looked at Olive's trailing 12-month token distribution and the proposed 120% trigger looks reasonable. Proposed construct: 

1) Term: 24 months. Year 1 commit (X tokens/month). Year 2 base = Year1_base + 10% (planned uplift).
2) Trigger: 3-month rolling window >120% of the month-by-month baseline (baseline is monthly average from prior 3 months adjusted for known seasonality).
3) Top-up mechanics: when trigger fires, automatically provision a temporary top-up bucket equal to 30% of that month’s usage for 3 months, billed monthly at a 15% premium to standard committed rate.
4) Annualization/floor: If after three months the client stays above 110% versus baseline, we propose rolling 50% of top-up into baseline at next annualization.
5) Capacity guarantees: Optional Dedicated burst blocks (recommended for mission-critical pipelines) — priced as reserved GPU-days per quarter.

I’m attaching a simple scenario table (SOW-upgrade-table.xlsx) that shows P&L for Olive across conservative/expected/optimistic growth.

Let me know what procurement/legal needs for wording — we can provide an amendment template with the trigger matrix and a definitions appendix.

-Karthik
